title: The Universal Testimony Of The Cosmos 18th Degree 2nd Truth Mutual Assistance

questions.question: What big picture does the passage give about what happens in autumn and spring in the whole world?
questions.answer: It says a large world seems to pass away in autumn, and a new one appears in spring.

questions.question: How are these changes in autumn and spring described?
questions.answer: They are described as happening in a careful, ordered, and regular way.

questions.question: What example is used to help us imagine the world?
questions.answer: The world is compared to a temporary resting place for travelers.

questions.question: In that comparison, what do living things do?
questions.answer: They stay for a while, do their jobs, and then leave.

questions.question: What does the passage say this order shows clearly to thinking people?
questions.answer: It shows that there is a glorious Creator with necessary existence, endless power, and lasting wisdom.

questions.question: What kind of worlds and realms does this Creator bring into existence?
questions.answer: He brings living realms and meaningful universes into being.

questions.question: For what kinds of purposes are these created things used?
questions.answer: They are used for Lordly purposes, Divine goals, and merciful aims.

questions.question: Which things are included in this truth of contingence?
questions.answer: Everything is included, whether great or small, general or specific, from the tiniest things to the largest.

questions.question: What does the passage say every created thing is given?
questions.answer: Each thing is given its own essence, shape, identity, qualities, and useful parts.

questions.question: Why is giving one exact form to a thing a sign of Allah’s power and wisdom?
questions.answer: Because many other forms were possible, yet the right one was chosen for it.

questions.question: Why is a thing’s special identity important in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that it was picked out and distinguished from many other possible members of its kind.

questions.question: What do suitable qualities and helpful organs show?
questions.answer: They show wise choice, great power, and deep wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do these many choices prove about the Creator?
questions.answer: They prove His necessary existence, infinite power, and unlimited wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s knowledge of things?
questions.answer: Nothing is hidden from Him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about difficulty for Allah?
questions.answer: Nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: What comparison is given to explain that great and small are equally easy for Allah?
questions.answer: Creating spring is said to be as easy for Him as creating a tree, and creating a tree as easy as creating a seed.

questions.question: What image does the passage give for the testimony of the universe?
questions.answer: It says the universe gives a great testimony with two wings and two truths.

questions.question: In this passage, which wing is being explained most directly?
questions.answer: The wing connected to createdness and contingence is being explained here.

questions.question: Why does the passage end this section briefly instead of giving every detail?
questions.answer: Because it says fuller explanations can be found elsewhere, so this long topic is being shortened here.

questions.question: What repeated pattern in nature is described at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The passing away of a world in autumn and the coming of a fresh one in spring.

questions.question: Does the passage present this pattern as random or planned? Explain.
questions.answer: It presents it as planned, because it happens with order, balance, and regularity.

questions.question: What lesson can a person learn from seeing many orderly deaths and new beginnings?
questions.answer: A person can learn that there is a powerful and wise Creator directing them.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the world to a place where travelers stop for a short time?
questions.answer: To show that living beings do not stay forever but come, serve a purpose, and move on.

questions.question: What three qualities of the Creator are especially clear in this section?
questions.answer: Necessary existence, infinite power, and unending wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Creator’s way of making things?
questions.answer: He makes them with wisdom, knowledge, order, and balance.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the purpose behind creation?
questions.answer: Creation has meaningful goals and merciful purposes.

questions.question: What is meant by saying contingence covers the whole universe?
questions.answer: It means all created things depend on being chosen and brought into existence.

questions.question: What range of things does the passage mention to show this truth is universal?
questions.answer: It includes everything from the highest to the lowest and from tiny atoms to huge planets.

questions.question: Name two special features the passage says each thing receives.
questions.answer: Each thing receives its own form and its own identity.

questions.question: Why does having one particular essence point to a chooser?
questions.answer: Because among many possibilities, one exact nature was selected.

questions.question: Why do helpful body parts count as evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they fit the creature’s needs wisely and beneficially.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that a creature gets the exact qualities it needs?
questions.answer: We can infer that its Maker knows it fully and chooses for it on purpose.

questions.question: What do the countless possibilities become in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: They become many signs and proofs of the Creator’s existence, power, and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s ability with large and small creations?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: Which examples are used to show that equal ease?
questions.answer: Spring and a tree, and a tree and a seed.

questions.question: What does the passage say about anything being hidden from Allah?
questions.answer: It says nothing at all is hidden from Him.

questions.question: What part does contingence play in the universe’s testimony?
questions.answer: It forms one wing of the universe’s great witness.

questions.question: What can a student understand from the phrase “two wings” in this passage?
questions.answer: The universe’s witness stands strongly on two connected truths, not just one.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The ordered changes in the world and the exact choosing of every created thing both point to Allah’s existence, power, and wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to the world in autumn?
questions.answer: A great world comes to an end.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens in spring?
questions.answer: A new world is brought forth.

questions.question: How often do these changes appear to happen?
questions.answer: They appear again and again in a repeated pattern.

questions.question: What does the careful pattern of these changes tell people who think deeply?
questions.answer: It tells them that a wise and powerful Creator is in control.

questions.question: What picture from everyday life is used to explain the world?
questions.answer: It is pictured as a lodging place for travelers.

questions.question: In that picture, what are “traveling worlds” and “migrant realms” doing?
questions.answer: They come, carry out their tasks, and then depart.

questions.question: What does this teach about life in this world?
questions.answer: It teaches that life here is temporary and purposeful.

questions.question: What qualities are mentioned to show the perfection of the Creator’s work?
questions.answer: Wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, and regularity.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention Divine aims and merciful goals?
questions.answer: To show that creation has meaning and kindness behind it.

questions.question: What truth is introduced after the discussion of createdness?
questions.answer: The truth of contingence.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the size or rank of things under this truth?
questions.answer: Every kind of thing falls under it, whether small or large, high or low.

questions.question: What are some things each being is specially given?
questions.answer: It is given a unique nature, shape, identity, qualities, and organs.

questions.question: Why is choosing one shape from many possibilities important?
questions.answer: It shows deliberate selection, not accident.

questions.question: Why is choosing one set of qualities from many options important?
questions.answer: It shows wisdom and knowledge in giving what fits best.

questions.question: What do these exact choices say about the Maker’s power?
questions.answer: They show that His power reaches all things without limit.

questions.question: What do they say about the Maker’s wisdom?
questions.answer: They show that He gives everything what suits it in the best way.

questions.question: What statement in the passage shows Allah’s complete knowledge?
questions.answer: It teaches that no thing and no matter is hidden from Him.

questions.question: How does the passage explain that Allah is not limited by the size of a task?
questions.answer: It says the biggest task is as easy for Him as the smallest.

questions.question: What are the three creation examples arranged from larger to smaller?
questions.answer: Spring, tree, and seed.

questions.question: What final role does this truth of contingence have in the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as one wing of the universe’s great testimony to Allah.

questions.question: What season is linked with the ending of a great world in the passage?
questions.answer: Autumn.

questions.question: What season is linked with the arrival of a fresh world?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: What words best describe how these seasonal changes happen?
questions.answer: They happen with order and regularity.

questions.question: Why is order in these changes important to the passage’s message?
questions.answer: Because order points to a Maker who acts with wisdom, not to blind chance.

questions.question: What comparison helps readers understand the short stay of living things in the world?
questions.answer: The world is compared to a stop for travelers.

questions.question: What do the travelers do before leaving, according to the comparison?
questions.answer: They complete their duties and move on.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage say all minds can see clearly?
questions.answer: That there is a glorious Being with necessary existence, infinite power, and endless wisdom.

questions.question: What are two things this glorious Being does in the world?
questions.answer: He creates living realms and brings purposeful universes into existence.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way He creates them?
questions.answer: With perfect wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, and regularity.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by contingence being everywhere?
questions.answer: It means every created thing depends on being chosen and specified by Allah.

questions.question: What is one sign of contingence found in every created thing?
questions.answer: Each one has its own exact form instead of countless other possible forms.

questions.question: What is another sign of contingence besides form?
questions.answer: Each thing also has a distinct identity and fitting qualities.

questions.question: Why do beneficial organs matter in this proof?
questions.answer: Because they are useful and suited to the creature, showing purposeful design.

questions.question: What does the passage say these many exact choices become?
questions.answer: They become signs and proofs pointing to Allah’s existence, power, and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah and hidden things?
questions.answer: Nothing is concealed from Him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah and difficult tasks?
questions.answer: No task is difficult for Him.

questions.question: Which comparison shows that huge creations and tiny creations are equally easy for Allah?
questions.answer: The making of spring compared with a tree, and a tree compared with a seed.

questions.question: If Allah can create a spring as easily as a tree, what does that suggest about His power?
questions.answer: It suggests His power is unlimited and not strained by greater size.

questions.question: What picture is used for the witness given by the universe?
questions.answer: It is pictured as a testimony with two wings.

questions.question: What main truth does this passage want readers to recognize?
questions.answer: The changing world and the exact design of every being both point clearly to Allah’s wise and powerful creation.

questions.question: What two seasons are used in the passage to show repeated change in the world?
questions.answer: Autumn and spring.

questions.question: What happens in autumn according to the passage?
questions.answer: A great world dies or passes away.

questions.question: What happens in spring according to the passage?
questions.answer: A new world is brought into being.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the many deaths and new creations inside this cycle?
questions.answer: It says they happen in a very orderly and regular way.

questions.question: What example from travel is used to describe the world?
questions.answer: It is described like an inn or stopping place for travelers.

questions.question: What do the visitors in that example do during their stay?
questions.answer: They remain for a time, carry out their work, and then continue on.

questions.question: What truth becomes clear from this ongoing order?
questions.answer: The existence of a glorious Creator with perfect power and wisdom becomes clear.

questions.question: Which qualities of that Creator are named in this section?
questions.answer: Necessary existence, infinite power, and unending wisdom.

questions.question: What kind of universes does the Creator bring into existence?
questions.answer: He brings forth living and purposeful universes.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention balance, order, and regularity together?
questions.answer: To show that creation is measured and controlled with wisdom.

questions.question: What truth about all created things is discussed after this?
questions.answer: The truth of contingence.

questions.question: What does the passage say all things are given when they enter the world?
questions.answer: They are given a certain nature, shape, identity, qualities, and useful organs.

questions.question: Why does one exact form among many possibilities point to a choosing Creator?
questions.answer: Because that form had to be selected from many other possible forms.

questions.question: Why does one exact identity among many similar beings matter?
questions.answer: Because it shows the being was specially distinguished and not left undefined.

questions.question: What do wise qualities and useful organs tell us?
questions.answer: They tell us there is wisdom and mercy in how creatures are made.

questions.question: What does the passage say these countless signs confirm?
questions.answer: They confirm Allah’s necessary existence, infinite power, and unlimited wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s knowledge of the universe?
questions.answer: Every object and every matter is known to Him.

questions.question: How does the passage explain Allah’s power by using spring, tree, and seed?
questions.answer: It says making the larger one is just as easy for Him as making the smaller one.

questions.question: What part of the universe’s witness does contingence form?
questions.answer: It forms one wing of the great witness of the cosmos.

questions.question: What is a good one-sentence summary of this passage?
questions.answer: The world’s orderly changes and the precise design of every creature show Allah’s existence, power, knowledge, and wisdom.

questions.question: What yearly change in the world does the passage ask us to notice?
questions.answer: It asks us to notice the end of a great world in autumn and the rise of a new one in spring.

questions.question: Is this change pictured as messy or well-arranged?
questions.answer: It is pictured as well-arranged.

questions.question: What does such arrangement lead people of understanding to realize?
questions.answer: It leads them to realize that a glorious and wise Creator exists.

questions.question: What simple comparison is used to explain the world’s temporary nature?
questions.answer: The world is compared to a place where travelers stay for a short time.

questions.question: In that comparison, why do beings leave after some time?
questions.answer: They leave after finishing the duties given to them.

questions.question: What three great qualities of the Creator are emphasized after this comparison?
questions.answer: His necessary existence, infinite power, and endless wisdom.

questions.question: What other qualities are shown in the way He creates?
questions.answer: His wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, and regularity are shown.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the purpose behind these creations?
questions.answer: They are made for meaningful Divine and merciful purposes.

questions.question: What is the next major truth discussed in the passage?
questions.answer: The truth of contingence.

questions.question: What does contingence tell us about created things?
questions.answer: It tells us they are not necessary by themselves and depend on Allah’s choosing and creating.

questions.question: Which kinds of things are included in this rule?
questions.answer: All things are included, whether tiny or huge, universal or particular.

questions.question: What are some examples of what each being is specially assigned?
questions.answer: It is assigned a certain essence, form, identity, attributes, and organs.

questions.question: Why is being given one exact identity a strong proof in the passage?
questions.answer: Because many other possibilities existed, yet one fitting identity was selected.

questions.question: How do useful organs strengthen the proof?
questions.answer: They show that creatures are equipped on purpose for benefit, not by accident.

questions.question: What do all these selections and assignments point to?
questions.answer: They point to Allah’s necessary existence, limitless power, and perfect wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s awareness of things?
questions.answer: It says nothing is hidden from Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s ability to do very large and very small things?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: Which examples are given to make that easier to understand?
questions.answer: The examples are spring, a tree, and a seed.

questions.question: What image does the passage use to describe how the universe points to Allah?
questions.answer: It uses the image of a great testimony with two wings.

questions.question: What is one wing made of in this passage?
questions.answer: It is made of the truth of contingence, together with the discussion of createdness in this section.

questions.question: Why might the passage mention that more details are explained elsewhere?
questions.answer: To show that this is a shortened explanation of a very large subject.
